title: BunTestOperandsV1
description: Which file operands of `bun test` are paths and which bun reads as FILTERS: only an operand starting with ./ or ../ (or .\ ..\ on Windows), an absolute path or a drive path is a path; any other operand makes bun scan the whole working directory (every directory held open until the scan ends: 122,880 descriptors and 2 GB in one measured case) and run nothing unless a file name matches its test patterns. A path that is the checkout or one of its parents has the same cost.

en.bare: [tests] `bun test {operand}` reads the operand as a filter, not as a path: bun would scan the whole working directory ({directory}), hold every directory open and run no test. Prefix it with ./ (as ./{operand}) or give the absolute path.
en.whole: [tests] `bun test {operand}` names the checkout or one of its parents: bun would scan every directory below it and hold each open. Name the test files (./path/to/file) or a narrower directory.

de.bare: [tests] `bun test {operand}` liest den Operanden als Filter, nicht als Pfad: bun würde das ganze Arbeitsverzeichnis ({directory}) durchsuchen, jedes Verzeichnis offen halten und keinen Test ausführen. Stelle ./ voran (als ./{operand}) oder gib den absoluten Pfad an.
de.whole: [tests] `bun test {operand}` nennt den Checkout oder eines seiner übergeordneten Verzeichnisse: bun würde jedes Verzeichnis darunter durchsuchen und offen halten. Nenne die Testdateien (./pfad/zur/datei) oder ein engeres Verzeichnis.
